newsitem.title: FRANCE: French trucks block refinery, Shell says no impact.
newsitem.headline: French trucks block refinery, Shell says no impact.

text.p: Striking French truck drivers blocked roads around the Royal Dutch/Shell oil refinery near Marseille on Wednesday, but the plant was carrying on as normal, a Shell spokesman in Paris said.
The drivers began blockading access roads near the Berre refinery in southern France on Tuesday, the spokesman said.
"There has been no impact on refinery operations for now," he said, adding that inside the complex everything was normal.
Berre, one of a cluster of refineries spread along the Mediterranean near Marseille, produces six million tonnes of oil products a year. It also has 14 separate petrochemical units.
Industry officials said the region's refineries -- others are operated by oil firms Total BP and Esso -- mainly depend on shipping and pipelines for their oil flows.
But trucks are used to supply to wholesale fuel depots and large retail outlets.
Berre is located near Marseille airport and is near a major motorway intersection heavily used by traffic.

Truck drivers were blocking roads across France for the third successive day on Wednesday and have promised to blockade fuel depots and cut supplies to supermarkets to press demands for wage hikes and shorter working hours.

Michel Caillot, head of the powerful National Truck Drivers Federation (FNCR), said after another failed round of talks with bosses that drivers had begun preventing tankers leaving oil refineries and fuel depots to cut supplies to petrol stations.
An FNCR spokeswoman said a depot was blocked in Bordeaux and plans were to block others near Nantes.
She said petrol stations and supermarkets kept low stocks and the blockade could start to bite within 48 hours.
Besides Shell France, other oil companies were not immediately available for comment.
